sources.title: AMD introduces new AI accelerators and networking solutions
sources.snippet:
AMD+0.22%

SAN FRANCISCO - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: NASDAQ:AMD) unveiled a suite of new products on Thursday aimed at enhancing AI infrastructure performance, including the AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators and networking components like the AMD Pensando Salina DPU and Pollara 400 NIC (NASDAQ:EGOV). These offerings are designed to meet the growing demands of AI applications and data centers. [...] The AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators, built on the AMD CDNA 3 architecture, promise to deliver significant improvements in AI performance, featuring 256GB of HBM3E memory and 6.0TB/s bandwidth. This represents an increase in memory capacity and bandwidth compared to previous models, with the MI325X offering 1.3 times the peak theoretical FP16 and FP8 compute performance. [...] AMD's growing presence in the cloud computing sector is further emphasized by its recent collaboration with Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). AMD's Instinct MI300X accelerators will power OCI's new AI supercluster, designed to handle complex AI workloads. Early adopters of this offering include Fireworks AI, which has effectively scaled its services using the enhanced memory capacity of the AMD Instinct MI300X.

sources.title: AMD vs NVIDIA AI GPU Market Share 2026: MI350X vs B200
sources.snippet:
The AI accelerator market is transitioning from NVIDIA monopoly to a three-tier competitive structure: NVIDIA retains 60–75% through 2028, AMD reaches 10–15% as the credible merchant silicon alternative, and custom silicon captures 15–25% concentrated in cloud-locked inference. All three can grow simultaneously because TAM is expanding from ~$200B to $500B+.

Both companies can win. Data as of April 2026. [...] NVIDIA holds approximately 80% of the AI accelerator market in 2026, with data center revenue reaching $193.7 billion in FY2026. AMD's Instinct GPU line generated an estimated $7–8 billion in 2025, capturing roughly 5–7% market share. However, the competitive landscape is more nuanced than a two-horse race: hyperscaler custom silicon (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom ASICs) collectively represents a larger and faster-growing threat to NVIDIA than AMD does. The AI accelerator total addressable [...] NVIDIA holds ~80% of the AI accelerator market by revenue with $193.7B in FY2026 data center sales, versus AMD's estimated 5-7% share (~$7-8B in Instinct revenue). AMD's MI350X matches B200 on FP8 compute (4,600 TFLOPS) and exceeds it on memory (288GB vs 192GB HBM3E), but NVIDIA's software maturity delivers 50-55% MFU versus AMD's ~45%, preserving a real-world performance gap. The bigger structural threat to NVIDIA is custom silicon — Broadcom AI ASIC revenue hit $20B+ in FY2025 — not AMD.

sources.title: Top 12 NVIDIA GPUs for AI Training & Inference in 2026
sources.snippet:
NVIDIA also provides workstation and consumer-grade GPUs, such as the RTX 6000 Ada Generation, RTX A6000, and GeForce RTX series. These are not purpose-built data center AI accelerators and rely on GDDR memory rather than HBM, but they can effectively support model experimentation, fine-tuning, and mid-scale inference at a lower cost.

When choosing AI infrastructure, organizations should focus on memory type and how well the system can scale: [...] Choose from the NVIDIA L40S GPU and NVIDIA H100 NVL to power generative AI workloads, train large language models (LLMs), and run high-throughput inference with strong memory bandwidth and multi-GPU scaling. While next-generation Blackwell GPUs with HBM3e lead frontier AI research, Atlantic.Net focuses on production-ready Hopper-based H100 NVL systems and balanced L40S accelerators that deliver reliable enterprise AI performance today. [...] NVIDIA AI GPUs empower developers to build and optimize a wide range of AI applications. These GPUs enable efficient training and deployment of machine learning models for tasks such as computer vision, natural language processing, and robotics.

Developers can utilize NVIDIA’s software stack, including CUDA, TensorRT, and the TAO Toolkit, to streamline workflows and improve performance. These tools facilitate model optimization, precision tuning, and integration into production environments.

sources.title: AMD Delivers Leadership AI Performance with AMD Instinct MI325X Accelerators
sources.snippet: Built on the AMD CDNA™ 3 architecture, AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators are designed for exceptional performance and efficiency for demanding AI tasks spanning foundation model training, fine-tuning and inferencing. Together, these products enable AMD customers and partners to create highly performant and optimized AI solutions at the system, rack and data center level. [...] SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 10, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) announced the latest accelerator and networking solutions that will power the next generation of AI infrastructure at scale: AMD Instinct™ MI325X accelerators, the AMD Pensando™ Pollara 400 NIC and the AMD Pensando Salina DPU. AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators set a new standard in performance for Gen AI models and data centers. Both companies are benefiting from sustained growth in AI infrastructure spending. [...] The AI chip market in August 2026 is characterized by sustained demand growth, intensifying competition, and evolving customer preferences. Enterprise customers are increasingly prioritizing vendor diversification, creating opportunities for AMD and other challengers to gain footholds in accounts previously dominated by Nvidia. This trend is particularly pronounced among hyperscale cloud providers, who are investing billions of dollars in AI infrastructure and seeking to mitigate supply chain [...] While Nvidia and AMD dominate the headlines, other players are making strategic moves in the AI chip market. Intel, despite losing market share in server CPUs to AMD, continues to invest heavily in AI accelerators and aims to regain relevance in the data center. The company Gaudi series represents its primary AI chip offering, though adoption has lagged behind Nvidia and AMD solutions.
